newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly to approve "lulus" on Tues - official.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly to approve "lulus" on Tues - official.

text.p: The New York Assembly is expected to approve on Tuesday a bill that will restore a total of about $62,500 in stipends, called "lulus," for a handful of members, a spokeswoman for the Speaker said.
"That will move today," said Pat Lynch, spokeswoman for Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan), who is the Assembly Speaker.
She explained the bill will restore the stipends that expired in November, and which were not approved by the legislature in its special session in late December.

The lulus became caught up in a political battle between Silver and the Senate Majority Leader, Joseph Bruno (D-Troy), who last week made the fight public, accusing the Speaker of holding up other bills, including a $12 billion highway capital program.
A spokesman for Bruno was not immediately available to comment.
Silver's spokeswoman said that on Thursday the highway construction bill was signed.
Another issue that had been held hostage in the fight over the lulus, the nomination of the new head of the bi-partisan, bill drafting commission, also was cleared.
And two bills dealing with medical centers in Westchester and Nassau Counties also are expected to be approved.
The Assembly Speaker's spokeswoman took pains to emphasize that Silver wanted to work cooperatively with his counterpart in the Senate, a position that echoed his statements last week.

"We have decided to move forward and not look behind us. This ties up loose ends from the December session. Everyone has agreed to move forward in a bipartisan way to address the needs of New Yorkers," she said.
